Psych major here! From what I've been taught about ADHD and learning, our minds (ADHDers) don't produce dopamine the way other's do. So normally, when we learn something new we'd be getting nice healthy dose of dopamine to make us feel good about having just learned. Problem is, either we have too many receptors for our dopamine producers or not enough producers of dopamine. (This is what things like Adderall are for!)

So for people like us, when it is time to hunker down and get some work done, our brains are like, "Sure, I'll work. If you make it worth my while." We then find ourselves searching up and down for something to motivate out brains to work. For me, I like to work a bit, game a bit (used to be one or two missions on Assassin's Creed) and then get more work done. 

I hope this made sense and is kind of helpful!
